clue.text: Means being enclosed in endless barrier

indicators.note: the phrase for being enclosed sits inside the shortened barrier word
endless tells us to drop the final letter of the barrier word

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
herewith is the formal letter-writing phrase for something enclosed alongside

explanation.surface: Someone trapped behind a wall that never seems to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being enclosed' looks like part of the picture of confinement, but it is the letter-writer's word for 'with this'. 'Endless' trims WALL to WAL, which goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherewithal is the money or resources needed, which is what 'means' signifies in 'a person of means'.

clue.text: He painted swine with deceit, ending with hospital

indicators.note: ending with places the hospital letter at the very end of the sequence

parts.note: a hog is a pig, a swine
art can mean cunning or trickery

explanation.surface: An artist painted pigs dishonestly, and ended up in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and engraver famous for satirical series such as A Rake's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth is a famous English painter, so 'he painted' describes him by example.

clue.text: Chains break cut by file

indicators.note: cut by means the break word is split open with the file word placed inside it

parts.note: a rest is a break
a train is a file or line of people or things moving in order

explanation.surface: A prisoner's chains are broken by a file smuggled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' suggests a metal tool for sawing chains, but here it is a line of people, as in 'single file'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are a means of physical restraint, so the word for restriction stands for them.

clue.text: What's actually gained earning salary initially

definitions.text: What's actually gained earning salary initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the first letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: A definition of take-home pay: the amount actually received from a salary.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells the answer from its initial letters and defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages are what a worker actually receives for work done, the money earned from employment.

clue.text: Shaping metal around vase with top of gold

indicators.note: around means the metal word wraps itself about the vase word

parts.note: tin is a metal
an urn is a vase

indicators.note: top of picks out the first letter of gold, the top of a down entry

explanation.surface: A craftsman shapes metal around a vase and tops it with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaping metal' reads as one phrase, like work on a lathe, but the definition is just 'Shaping'; 'metal' is TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning is shaping wood or metal on a lathe, so it is a kind of shaping.

clue.text: Giant iguanas covering island

indicators.note: covering means the phrase giant iguanas wraps around the island's name inside it

explanation.surface: Enormous lizards blanket a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Head express keeping in charge of train

parts.note: dome is slang for the head

indicators.note: keeping in means the express word holds the charge abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to state is to express
IC stands for in charge

explanation.surface: A head of rail operations runs an express service while keeping control of the train.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway words 'express' and 'train' are both misleading: 'express' is the verb STATE, and 'train' means to tame.
explanation.definitionFit: To domesticate an animal is to tame and train it to live with people.

clue.text: Beggar you heard is wrapped in Telegraph?

indicators.note: is wrapped in means the spoken word goes inside the newspaper word

parts.note: the Telegraph is a newspaper, a paper

indicators.note: heard signals that the letter is a sound-alike of the word you

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: A beggar asks whether you were told he sleeps wrapped in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is the British daily newspaper that published this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper is a very poor person, one who might have to beg.

clue.text: Fruit variety with very big exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the size abbreviation forms the outside, around the variety word

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a range is a variety, as in a range of goods

explanation.surface: A variety of fruit with a huge outer skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruit, so they are examples of fruit.

clue.text: Pirouette gradually losing core speed

indicators.note: losing core means everything between the first and last letters of gradually goes

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: A dancer's spin slowly loses speed at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin round and round, as a dancer does in a pirouette.

clue.text: Unusually spine's erect showing determination

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: here the apostrophe is ignored and its S counts as a letter of the anagram

explanation.surface: Holding one's back unusually straight shows grit.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of spine's does supply a letter: the eleven letters of SPINES ERECT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistence is continuing firmly despite difficulty, which is determination.

clue.text: Sovereign consumed by temper, originally

indicators.note: consumed by means the ruler's title is swallowed up inside the words temper originally

explanation.surface: A monarch whose original nature was overwhelmed by rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letter signal, but it simply supplies the last letters of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler, so a sovereign in the general sense of a monarch.

clue.text: Pebbles unbroken round end of beach

indicators.note: round means the unbroken word goes around the letter from the beach

parts.note: single can mean whole or undivided, as in a single sheet

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of beach

explanation.surface: Pebbles that stay whole lying around at the far end of the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, especially on a beach.

clue.text: Light seen from church on mountain

indicators.note: on here means the church letters come after the mountain word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: A light visible from a church high on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, a word common in southwest England such as on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light, a flame or battery lamp you can carry.

clue.text: Chinese characters, say, creating a grid some decrypted

indicators.note: decrypted means the letters are worked out of their coded order into new sense

explanation.surface: Code-breakers make a grid in which some Chinese script is cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideograms are written symbols standing for ideas; Chinese characters are the standard example, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Try and goal always, we hear, follows

indicators.note: follows means the sounded always word comes after the goal word

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

indicators.note: we hear signals that the always word is entered as a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Rugby talk: a try, then a goal kicked every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' and 'goal' read like rugby scoring. In a British accent EVER and EAVOUR sound alike, so END plus the sound-alike gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard, and as a noun it is an attempt.

clue.text: Thought about love, inhibited about sex

parts.note: C stands for circa, about
love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scoring

indicators.note: the second about means the inhibited word goes around the sex word

parts.note: gated means confined to one's home or college as a punishment
it is a common slang term for sex

explanation.surface: Someone pondered love but was too shy to talk about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thought about' looks like the definition, but 'about' is C. To be gated is to be grounded, a British school and college punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply, so cogitated is a past tense of thinking.

clue.text: Allure left French love after midnight

indicators.note: after puts the left letter and the French word after the midnight letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G
amour is French for love

explanation.surface: The French charm of a lover who left after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is an attractive, exciting quality, the same as allure or charm.

clue.text: Undecided purchasing endlessly expensive hat

indicators.note: purchasing means the undecided word takes in, or acquires, the shortened rich word

parts.note: torn means undecided, as in torn between two options

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter from the word for expensive

parts.note: rich can mean costly or expensive, as rich food or fabrics

explanation.surface: A shopper wavers over buying a hat that seems endlessly pricey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchasing' is read as taking in: the undecided word takes in the shortened word for expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat of the 18th century.

clue.text: Fish held on board ship

indicators.note: on board means the held word sits inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
had means held, as in had in one's hand

explanation.surface: Fish caught and kept on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Shads are herring-like fish, so they are examples of fish.

clue.text: Fly in bridge partners for a bit

indicators.note: in means the fly goes between the bridge partner letters

parts.note: in the card game bridge, South and North, S and N, play as partners
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: A fly pesters the bridge partners for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a bit' suggests a stretch of time; the definition is 'a bit', a small amount, with 'for' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, so a little bit.

clue.text: Trouble on Navy's decks

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the trouble word above the navy letters

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out on the decks of the Navy's ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decks' looks like ships' decks but is the verb, as in decking the halls.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, so adorns, embellishes, matches decks as a verb.

clue.text: Finding time's flying

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time; the 's stands for is, a link
racing means speeding, flying along

explanation.surface: Discovering how time flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing something is tracking it down, so it means finding, as in tracing a lost relative.

clue.text: Band Queen in rise

indicators.note: in means the queen letter goes inside the rise phrase

parts.note: go up means rise
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A band called Queen rising up the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band, but it is the Latin abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of musicians or of people is a group.

clue.text: Fat detective's gripped by a role

indicators.note: gripped by means the detective letters are held inside a and the role word

parts.note: a pose is an assumed role or act
DI is a detective inspector; the 's means is, a link

explanation.surface: An overweight detective is consumed by a part he plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means relating to fat, as in adipose tissue, the body's fatty tissue.

clue.text: Flamboyant men turning over palm

indicators.note: over puts the turned letters ahead of the palm word
turning means the men letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers, so men
the coco is the coconut palm

explanation.surface: Showy men flipping over a palm tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate 18th-century style, so the word describes anything flamboyant and elaborate.

clue.text: Natural gold and silver turned almost delicate

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: turned means the silver symbol is read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the delicate word

parts.note: nice can mean delicate or subtle, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: Gold and silver worked into delicate natural shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' makes GA from AG, and 'almost' trims NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is natural, grown without artificial chemicals.

clue.text: Sheer pants aren't fashionable to have run in

indicators.note: to have, with in, means the rearranged letters take the run letter inside
in completes the instruction to place the run letter within the rearranged letters
fashionable is read as fashion-able, able to be fashioned, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: See-through trousers aren't stylish to go jogging in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' rearranges the letters of 'pants' to TANSP, and R goes in after the T; the apostrophe of 'aren't' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is so thin it is see-through, which is transparent.
